Definition: from the same as G2276; to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower:--be inferior, overcome.
BiblicalUsage: Hēttáō means to make worse, to vanquish — to get the better of someone. It turns up 3 times, in 2 Corinthians and 2 Peter, where being overcome is the picture of defeat.
TheologicalSignificance: I take hēttáō as it stands — to make worse, to vanquish — and I read the passages with that plain sense in mind.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
